name: Y-Intersection
spec: yellow diamond with a black Y-shaped symbol
meaning: The road splits ahead into two branches.

snippets.back: At any intersection you must stop for a blind person using a guide dog or holding out a red-tipped white cane.
The warning-sign examples identify intersections, signals, merges, wet-road skidding hazards, lane endings, schools, and pedestrian crossings.
Red, yellow and green signal lights stand at many intersections to control the direction and flow of traffic.
Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, who have the right-of-way at every intersection and crosswalk; come to a full stop and let them pass safely.
A Y-intersection warning means the route divides and the driver must bear right or left.
At the approach of an emergency vehicle, pull to the nearest road edge at once and stop until it passes, keeping every intersection clear.

You must not pass within one hundred feet of or while crossing any intersection or railroad crossing, nor within one hundred feet of a posted narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, and the end of a no passing zone only means visibility has improved, not that passing is safe.
Slow at every intersection and hunt for devices, crossing traffic, walkers and cyclists, road conditions, and blind corners, trusting no one to obey or yield.
